questions.question_text: When it is $10{:}00\text{ am}$ in London ($\text{UTC}+0$), what is the local time in Tokyo ($\text{UTC}+9$)?

options.why: Subtracted $9\text{ hours}$ instead of adding for Tokyo.
Added 9 to 12 instead of the given 10 am.
Failed to convert 19:00 to 7:00 pm, labelling it as morning.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = 9 - 0 = 9\text{ hours}$
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Time in Tokyo} = 10{:}00 + 9\text{ hours} = 19{:}00 = 7{:}00\text{ pm}$.

questions.question_text: When it is $11{:}00\text{ am}$ on Wednesday in Sydney ($\text{UTC}+10$), what is the local day and time in Vancouver ($\text{UTC}-8$)?

options.why: Forgot to subtract a day when rolling back across midnight.
Added $18\text{ hours}$ instead of subtracting for a western location.
Subtracted $20\text{ hours}$ instead of $18\text{ hours}$.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = -8 - 10 = -18\text{ hours}$
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Time in Vancouver} = 11{:}00 - 18\text{ hours} = -7{:}00$
4. **Adjust for midnight rollover (subtract 24 hours for next day, add 24 hours for previous day)**
$-7{:}00 + 24{:}00 = 17{:}00\text{ on Tuesday} = 5{:}00\text{ pm on Tuesday}$.

questions.question_text: A flight leaves Auckland ($\text{UTC}+12$) at $3{:}00\text{ pm}$ on Friday, flying to Los Angeles ($\text{UTC}-8$). The flight takes $12\text{ hours}$. What is the local day and time in Los Angeles when the plane arrives?

options.why: Added $20\text{ hours}$ time difference instead of subtracting for Los Angeles.
Failed to roll back date to Thursday before adding flight time.
Subtracted the flight time instead of adding it.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = -8 - 12 = -20\text{ hours}$
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in LA} = 15{:}00\text{ Friday} - 20\text{ hours} = -5{:}00 = 19{:}00\text{ on Thursday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival in LA} = 19{:}00\text{ (Thursday)} + 12\text{ hours} = 31{:}00$
4. **Adjust for midnight rollover (subtract 24 hours for next day, add 24 hours for previous day)**
$31{:}00 - 24{:}00 = 07{:}00\text{ on Friday} = 7{:}00\text{ am on Friday}$.

questions.question_text: A non-stop flight departs London ($\text{UTC}+0$) at $10{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Sunday for Singapore ($\text{UTC}+8$). The flight duration is $13\text{ hours}$. What is the local day and time in Singapore upon arrival?

options.why: Forgot to add the $8\text{ hours}$ time difference for Singapore.
Subtracted $8\text{ hours}$ instead of adding for an eastern destination.
Added 8 hours twice during the calculation.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
Singapore is $8\text{ hours}$ ahead of London.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in Singapore} = 22{:}30\text{ Sunday} + 8\text{ hours} = 30{:}30 = 06{:}30\text{ on Monday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival in Singapore} = 06{:}30\text{ (Monday)} + 13\text{ hours} = 19{:}30 = 7{:}30\text{ pm on Monday}$.

questions.question_text: A passenger flies from Mumbai ($\text{UTC}+5.5$) to Sydney ($\text{UTC}+10$). Sydney is $4.5\text{ hours}$ ahead of Mumbai. The flight departs Mumbai at $1{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Saturday, stops for a $2\text{-hour}$ layover in Singapore, and arrives in Sydney at $8{:}30\text{ am}$ on Sunday. What was the total flying time?

options.why: Included the 2-hour layover in the flying time.
Subtracted the time difference from Mumbai time instead of adding it.
Subtracted 4 hours instead of 2 for the layover.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
Sydney is $4.5\text{ hours}$ ahead of Mumbai.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in Sydney time} = 13{:}30 + 4\text{ h } 30\text{ min} = 18{:}00\text{ on Saturday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Total elapsed time} = 18{:}00\text{ Saturday to } 08{:}30\text{ Sunday} = 14\text{ h } 30\text{ min}$
$\text{Total flying time} = 14\text{ h } 30\text{ min} - 2\text{ hours (layover)} = 12\text{ h } 30\text{ min}$.

questions.question_text: A transport aircraft departs Point $A(15^{\circ}\text{N}, 30^{\circ}\text{W})$ at $7{:}00\text{ am}$ on Tuesday, flying to Point $B(20^{\circ}\text{N}, 60^{\circ}\text{E})$. The flight duration is $7\text{ hours}$. Using $15^{\circ} = 1\text{ hour}$, what is the local time in Point $B$ when the aircraft arrives?

options.why: Subtracted the $6\text{-hour}$ time difference instead of adding for an eastern destination.
Added flight time but forgot to apply the longitude time difference.
Calculated time difference using latitude instead of longitude.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Longitude difference} = 60^{\circ} + 30^{\circ} = 90^{\circ}$
$\text{Time difference} = \dfrac{90^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}} = 6\text{ hours}$
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in Point } B = 07{:}00 + 6\text{ hours} = 13{:}00$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival time} = 13{:}00 + 7\text{ hours} = 20{:}00 = 8{:}00\text{ pm on Tuesday}$.

questions.question_text: A passenger departs Adelaide ($\text{ACST } \text{UTC}+9.5$) at $10{:}00\text{ am}$ on Thursday, stops for $3\text{ hours}$ in Singapore, and arrives in Mumbai ($\text{UTC}+5.5$) at $8{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Thursday. What was the total flying time?

options.why: Included the 3-hour layover in the flying time.
Subtracted the time difference twice.
Calculated elapsed time without converting to Mumbai local departure time.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
Mumbai is $9.5 - 5.5 = 4\text{ hours}$ behind Adelaide.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in Mumbai time} = 10{:}00\text{ am} - 4\text{ hours} = 06{:}00\text{ am}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Total elapsed time} = 06{:}00\text{ to } 20{:}30 = 14\text{ h } 30\text{ min}$
$\text{Total flying time} = 14\text{ h } 30\text{ min} - 3\text{ hours (layover)} = 11\text{ h } 30\text{ min}$.

questions.question_text: An international flight departs Point $A(25^{\circ}\text{S}, 150^{\circ}\text{E})$ at $10{:}00\text{ pm}$ on Friday for Point $B(38^{\circ}\text{N}, 120^{\circ}\text{W})$. The flight takes $14\text{ hours}$. Using $15^{\circ} = 1\text{ hour}$, what is the local day and time in Point $B$ upon arrival?

options.why: Forgot to subtract a day when adjusting by the 18-hour time difference.
Added 18 hours instead of subtracting for a western destination.
Found the departure time in Point B but forgot to add the 14-hour flight duration.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Longitude difference} = 150^{\circ} - (-120^{\circ}) = 270^{\circ}$
$\text{Time difference} = \dfrac{270^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}} = 18\text{ hours}$
Point $B$ ($120^{\circ}\text{W}$) is $18\text{ hours}$ behind Point $A$ ($150^{\circ}\text{E}$).
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$10{:}00\text{ pm Friday} = 22{:}00$
$\text{Departure in Point } B = 22{:}00\text{ Friday} - 18\text{ hours} = 04{:}00\text{ on Friday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival in Point } B = 04{:}00\text{ (Friday)} + 14\text{ hours} = 18{:}00 = 6{:}00\text{ pm on Friday}$.
